steps.text: Combine milk and vinegar in a small bowl; set aside for 10 minutes for milk to curdle and thicken.

Pour heavy cream into a clean glass jar. Stir in curdled milk. Cover jar loosely with cheesecloth to allow mixture to breathe and coagulate; let stand at room temperature for 24 hours. Chill before using and store leftovers in the refrigerator in a covered container for up to 1 week.

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Sour Cream
raw_recipe.description: Homemade sour cream made with milk, vinegar, and cream that tastes just like store-bought! Best to make this easy recipe the night before you need it.
raw_recipe.name: Homemade Sour Cream

review.reviewBody: Very good recipe, I didn't feel comfortable leaving a jar of cream and milk out even though the vinegar was probably enough to kill bacteria, I cheated I mixed it up with my kitchen aid until it looked like sour cream, and turned out tasting great plus I added a pinch of salt. Thank you for the recipe. 5 stars all the way!

This works like a charm- very thick and rich! Sterilize your Mason jar. I used buttermilk and a good quality heavy (high butterfat) cream. Secure the lid and canning ring, shake, and let sit on the counter for 24 hours, undisturbed! We can now taste the difference between home made and store bought, and will be using this recipe from here on!

like another reviewer, I was not comfortable leaving this sit out overnight. I downsized the recipe to 3/4 cup cream, 3 T milk and 1/2 tsp white vinegar, whizzed it in the magic bullet for maybe 10 seconds total, and this is sour cream!!!! so handy as I had cream on hand but not sour cream, now I can make one of the mashed potato recipes from this site that look so good and call for sour cream. thank you!!!!!

This recipe came in handy not too long ago. I only give it 4 stars because I had to make a few tweaks. It takes about 48 hours for me for the texture to be nearly spot on. At that point I salt to taste and serve. I never knew how easy it was to make sour cream! I am really glad I found this recipe. Thank you for sharing.

*Note- I have made this many times and once tried salting the sour cream at the beginning of the process and it seems to cause it to be super runny. Just FYI.

Awesome sour cream! This sour cream is so easy to make. I use buttermilk. I am talking real buttermilk, not the wimpy low fat stuff. One cup of heavy cream and 1/4 cup buttermilk, stir together, cover loosely and let sit on the counter. I let mine sit for approx 11 hours because my husband doesn't like anything that tastes sour or tangy. He has not liked sour cream in all of his 59 years but now eats my sour cream. I can not recommend this recipe more!

I have made this recipes several times typically using buttermilk and heavy whipping cream. Here’s the caveat, depending on the temperature and humidity levels, It may take a little bit longer to thicken up. I put mine in the oven with the light on for at least 24 hours, depending on how sour you like it, mine is always thick luscious and perfect. The only reason I’m even bothering to leave a review is because there seems to be so many bad ones. I’ve never had this recipe go bad except for the time my husband accidentally turned the oven on and baked it lol

This worked like a charm. I used ultra pasteurized heavy cream, ultra pasteurized whole milk and I cleaned my jar with scalding hot water before using it. I also added a pinch of salt.

After 24 hours with the mixture sitting on the counter, it was still the consistency of milk. So I waited another 24 hours with the covered mixture still sitting on the counter. This time the consistency was a soft cream and the flavor was excellent: much better than store bought sour cream.

The next time I make this I will wait until consistency is a little thicker still. I might also add a few drops of lemon juice, but the buttermilk flavor is quite pleasing all by itself.

Loving sour cream as I do I thought let’s try! I did (but tweaked a bit) and it’s fabulous! HOWEVER…I used 1/4 c buttermilk instead of the vinegar/milk combo and let it sit about 33 hours and it’s fantastic! Also I thought it would be a fail as I read later so not use ULTRA pasteurized HWC and that’s all I have but it turned out terrific!!

I made the recipe as listed, left at room tempurature for 24 hours, then refrigerated for 24 hours. it had a slight twang, but wasn't thickening. I added 1 Tbsp of lime juice and whipped the cream to just short of stiff peaks. it tastes like sour cream and has nearly the same consistency as store bought, just more airy. Awesome recipe, just needed some adjustments to be complete.

I used 1 cup heavy cream, 1 cup buttermilk, 1 TBSP lemon juice, 1/4 tsp of kosher salt. Covered tightly & left out of refrigerator for 48 hours. It’s SOUR cream, so leaving out of fridge makes sense! Sooooooo creamy and delicious!

Recipe turned out very well! 

We keep our house pretty cold during the winter, so it did take a little over two days on the counter to get firm, but it is now nearly as thick store bought (I can hold it upside down). It'll probably go faster in summer. I also found recipes online that whipped theirs for "instant" sour cream, so if yours comes out runny, whip it a little. 
I used ACV because it's healthier, and I have it on hand since I make that also. I added extra at the end because there wasn't a strong enough flavor for me, (pure preference - I like it very tangy) and a big pinch of salt. Tastes pretty good! As for it not working because of various "science" reasons - it works. Mine thickened (with a little extra time). Soured. And, even after being on the counter for two days, didn't make anyone sick.
Simple and well worth it. (Can't understand why a reviewer dramatically changed the recipe, then gave it 4 stars though.)

So tried this with keeping it out of the refrigerator for 48 hrs and then put it in the refrigerator. We didn’t have a mixer at the time so couldn’t try this as some others recommended but after about 1 week longer I the fridge it actually thickened up pretty nicely and my kids loved it but I’m not sure why or how the recipe is supposed to work in 24 hrs.
This recipe works for me. I had to use chilled heavy cream. I added some more ingredients to suit my taste. 1) a pinch of salt 2) 3-4drops of freshly squeezed lemon juice 3) a pinch of garlic powder

What the recipe doesn't say is to not use ultra pasturized milk and cream. If you can find unpasturized milk or pasturized without ultra in front of it then thats what you need. Also add a pinch of salt. Or like others said you can use butter milk which the vinegar & milk is a substitute for.

I have used sour milk using white vinegar for a substitute for buttermilk for ages. Buttermilk is just not a good as it used to be, just read the label. So I was glad to see this recipe for sour cream. Thank you. It works just fine.
Hopefully, around 9:30/9:45p on tomorrow, I can have a nice baked potato. I'm super excited! Wondering if I can leave it on a table as it sits until tomorrow night... :/

I used what I had to work with and served it same day. 

Cool Whip
Distilled White Vinegar
Milk
Plain Powdered Creamer
Worked great!
